It was a thunderstorm the night that "Cardinal Dimanche" came to us. He stood in the sanctuary of the church, untouched by the gale that raged outside.
That should have served as my first cause for concern. Instead, I bowed my head to him and greeted him as I would any new envoy from the Holy Mother.
We had been expecting a new Cardinal since our last one had departed several months earlier from illness, after all.
Dimanche greeted me with a warm smile and a firm handshake. I asked him if his journey was long. I will never forget his reply.
"It was difficult... but it was not long."
It puzzled me at the time, as did the fact that his greatcoat was bone dry. But I dismissed it, as all are wont to do when one is faced with the unusual.
And I did not have time to consider it, as Marie in her eagerness arrived a moment later.
He knelt down to greet her at her level in her chair, and took her hands in his. I should have seen the manipulation for what it was.
He was not the only devil to arrive on our doorstep in a storm, after all.
